title: Independent leaf occurrences in an integral-system expression
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme and let $V$ be a finite well-typed expression in pullback, proper direct image, quasi-compact open extension, compactification support and tensor, with its variable schemes over $B$, as in [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain]. Define the set $\operatorname{Occ}(V)$ of individual leaf occurrences recursively: a variable has one occurrence, a unary operation retains the occurrences of its operand, and a tensor has the disjoint union of the occurrences of its two operands. Each occurrence retains its original variable scheme over $B$. Reindex the expression by this finite occurrence set, replacing each leaf by its own independent variable and preserving every operation, morphism, proper/open witness and compactification. An original family of inputs gives the occurrence family by repeating each input at its occurrences; maps of input families act by the same repeated component maps, defining the occurrence-input functor. In categories with integer shift [def-weil-triangulated-category], define the shift of an occurrence family at $(i,r)$ by replacing only the value at occurrence $i$ by its shift by $r\in\mathbf Z$. Repeated occurrences of the same object remain independently indexed. Variable renaming acts recursively on the existing expression type. Fixing all other occurrence values defines the unary slot context, retaining the side of every tensor vertex. Its evaluation at any replacement object is canonically identified, by equality, with evaluation of the independently indexed expression at the family updated at precisely that occurrence. The single-occurrence shift is also the endofunctor of input families which evaluates and shifts precisely that component and evaluates every other component; its object family is the stated dependent update. The original input label of an occurrence is recorded recursively. Independent relabelling has a bijective leaf-label map, so independently labelled expressions are precisely expressions equipped with this bijectivity condition; every original expression has this presentation. For an independently labelled expression, searching for its unique occurrence of a given input label returns the corresponding single-slot context. Evaluating this context on a replacement P equals evaluating the original expression with just that input replaced; at its original value it equals the original evaluation. The product-family shift is defined once for any indexed family of categories and then specialized to the occurrence family; its object action is the same dependent update.

proof.text: For inputShift_obj apply dependent function extensionality at j and split on i = j. Substitution in the equal case and Function.update_of_ne in the unequal case identify the product-functor component with the dependent update. The occurrence-functor object theorem is this equality specialized to the occurrence family.

Prove the private evaluation-under-renaming equality by induction on the expression: evaluation of reindexInputs f at K is evaluation of the old tree at K composed with f. Then induct on the original tree for slotContext_evaluate. Unary cases apply congrArg of the unchanged operation. At a tensor split the selected occurrence into the left or right summand, apply the renaming equality and the selected induction hypothesis, and check dependent updates componentwise. The other summand is unchanged.

By induction, reindexing preserves the occurrence set up to an explicit equivalence, and the renamed occurrence label is f applied to the original label through that equivalence. At each tensor take the sum of these equivalences. Induct on the tree to prove independentInputs_bijectiveLabel: the variable case is the singleton bijection, unary cases preserve it, and the tensor case composes the sum equivalence with the disjoint sum of the inductive label bijections.

Induct on the expression to characterize a successful variableContext search by existence of a leaf with the requested label. At a tensor search the left tree first; if it fails, the existence statement reduces to the right tree. Surjectivity proves variableContext_isSome. Separately, induction shows that updating a label absent from a tree leaves its evaluation unchanged. Finally induct along a successful search under injectivity of the leaf-label map: in the selected tensor branch use the induction hypothesis and in the other branch use the absence lemma; injectivity excludes the same label in both branches. This proves evaluation on any replacement. Apply it also at the original value and use Function.update_eq_self for the second equality.
